html:
Salla Drennen (I28)

Region in the English rating survey: Escann.

In one sentence: Protect a weak clan amid the Thorn Grove, kinship blood feuds and fey agreements, then turn a defensive community into an organiser of the Verdant Pact.

Story: very high | Mission-tree length: long (22 unique and 14 shared Wood Elf missions) | Mission-tree currency: a dedicated tree exists in the current local version | Distinctiveness: very high | Grind: medium-high | Early pressure: high | Expansion capacity: moderate

Identity and history

Salla Drennen is a Wood Elf clan of the Thorn Grove in the western Deepwoods, Tag I28, with its capital at Drennethílle. It follows the Fey Court and is ruled in 1444 by young Narawen Drennen. [Local history; localisation] The history gives her powerful magic, the Kind-Hearted and Silver Tongue traits, and historical friendships with several Wood Elf clans. This is not an opening that overwhelms neighbours through military strength, but a fragile community surviving through diplomacy and its ties to the fey. [Local history]

The offline Wiki describes Drennen elves as the clans' closest neighbours to the fey: entire villages may enter the Feyrealm and return days or years later. Arun Drennen's experiments killed Eledas in 1428, setting off the Cousins' War; an orc invasion in 1430 then killed Narawen's parents. After succeeding them, she sought fey assistance and later convened the Conclave of Elynáile in 1442–1443, advancing the Verdant Pact. This is the Wiki's pre-opening chronology. Local friendship flags are not equated with the date of that conclave. [Wiki]

National story and campaign arc

The dedicated missions begin with the thorns taking root: establish Drennen's ranger camp, then advance out of the hills. During the crisis, words, kinship and allies must become usable political resources. Mission prose does not simply declare Arun's guilt resolved; it continues to ask how Drennen protects the clan, rebuilds community and deals with old feuds. [Local scripts; narrative text]

The middle phase joins the shared Wood Elf line: the Verdant Path, Verdant Pact, refugee settlement, capital development, a verdant army, recovering land and ending the Greentide threat. The parsed structure contains 22 distinct missions in the I28-specific file and 14 missions in WoodElves_Missions.txt explicitly including I28. The 31 I28_* definition blocks in the Salla file include 9 column containers and cannot be counted as 31 missions. The final I28_the_pact_fufilled and I28_the_pact_fufilled_real have different IDs and hidden/revealed conditions: the former requires I28_reveal to be absent and the latter requires it to be present. Each is indexed once; they are neither duplicate IDs nor both necessarily visible in one state. The unique line continues through blood and bone, kinship promises, fey and the Veil. Completing I28_blood_and_bone triggers unique advisers and inherit = I29; I28_restoring_the_bonds adds I28_veil_resonance and sets I28_reveal. [Local scripts; events]

The endgame has two layers. First, survive within the pact as a weak clan, preserve autonomy, repair kinship and repel orc and goblin threats. Second, a completed Verdant Pact route can form Cyranvar I45, changing Tag and replacing non-generic missions. The successor's content must not be projected backwards into I28's opening. Drennen is a Deepwoods prelude within a continuous campaign. [Local decisions; scripts]

Core mechanics

The first defining system is Deepwoods geography and the Verdant Pact. Shared missions connect recovery, refugee settlement, clan diplomacy and defence against the Greentide. Community explanations of ending thresholds and timing are version-sensitive experience; current scripts remain the authority. [Local scripts; community opinion]

The second is kinship and fey politics. Historical friendships, Narawen's spells, fey-relationship variables and I28's missions together create a diplomatic loop. Armies cannot solve everything. Ranger camps and forest defence are also concrete prerequisites of the first unique mission. [Local history; scripts]

Gameplay by stage

Begin by protecting Narawen and the capital, using historical friendships and clan diplomacy to contain stronger neighbours. Prepare a counterattack through the ranger camp and forest routes. Against orcs, goblins and the Greentide, balance recovering clan lands, allied or subject arrangements and the pact window.

The middle game follows the interlocking prerequisites of I28's unique missions and the shared Wood Elf tree. Capital development, refugee settlement, the verdant army, counterattacks and kinship commitments need attention together. Blood And Bone actually leads to I29's annexation, while the relationship-repair mission requires high relations with I30 and I33, restores their core provinces to Wood Elf culture and the Fey Court, and creates mutual historical friendships. These effects demonstrate different political treatment; neither should be advertised as every player's inevitable ending. [Local missions]

Later, forming Cyranvar changes the focus from clan survival to Deepwoods unification. Remaining I28 allows the Drennen-specific fey, Veil and kinship story to continue. A formation-driven tree change marks a new phase, not an unrelated second starting-country card.

Personality and recommendations

The v2.1 coordinates are expansion 65/100 | autocracy 40/100 | magic–artifice direction 82/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 74/100) | pluralism 78/100.

Its v2.1 values classification is Good (72/100), with a stable trajectory. The coordinates—expansion 65 / autocracy 40 / magic direction 82 (theme intensity 74) / pluralism 78—describe expansion serving clan recovery and ending the Greentide, rather than annexation alone. Clan councils, kinship and allies constrain power. The Fey Court, fey relations, the Veil and powerful mages make magic central to both story and missions; the Verdant Pact and refugee settlement support a high pluralism coordinate. [Local scripts; history]

The provisional value assessment is Good, 72/100: dignity 70, public good 78, personhood 80 and restraint 55 produce a weighted 72.25, rounded to 72. Clan protection, refugees, inter-clan agreements and a cooperative path provide positive evidence. Blood feuds, warfare and fighting invaders do not themselves reduce the score. The full treatment of residents and consequences of fey policies are not established, so confidence is not raised. The trajectory remains stable, with medium confidence. Political paths and fey relations change, but annexation or land return alone do not demonstrate a moral reversal; unconfirmed population policies are not used as deductions.

Recommended for players who enjoy character relationships, Deepwoods diplomacy and reversing a weak opening. Avoid it if you want a straight conquest line, intend to disregard clan relationships or dislike managing formation deadlines.

Community experience and evidence boundaries

Two player discussions directly mention Drennen: a development-version thread dated 2026-01-18 calls the campaign enjoyable, while a guide dated 2023-12-08 uses I28 to discuss releasing other clans before the Verdant Pact ends. The former explicitly concerns a development version but gives no commit; neither declares submods. They supply version-sensitive experience, not current thresholds or rewards. [Community opinion] Official Dev Diary #88, Tales from the Deepwoods, supplies regional context only. See the original evidence page for counting conventions, actual source lines and gaps, and the English source-text receipt for this translation's checks.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Salla Drennen (I28) — Salla Drennen Ideas

Set ID: I28_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = I28 #Salla Drennen
    }

Drennen Traditions

  • Religious power modifier: +10% (church_power_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Hostile Attrition: +100% (hostile_attrition; raw value 1).

1. Thorns and Vines

Plantlife within the Thorn Grove is stronger than anywhere else in the Deepwoods. Tangled roots choke the ground, moss and lichen carpet every surface, and thorny bushes and vines make traversal a challenging affair. Every settlement within Salla Drennen is built behind countless lines of natural defences, living and growing; a wall of wood and thorns as strong as any rampart or parapet.

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

2. Closest to the Fey

Among Cannorians, Wood Elves are often seen as a strange, wild, fey-touched people, who dance around fairy rings and whose forest might as well be the feyrealm itself. Among the Wood Elves, this reputation belongs to clan Drennen.

It is a reputation not unwarranted though, for the line between the material plane and the feyrealm is especially thin in the Thorn Grove, even more so than in the other groves of the Deepwoods. So close indeed is the connection, that whole villages of Drennen elves are sometimes lost for days, phased into the feyrealm. But they always return. A testament to the truth, that while every Wood Elf knows and respects the fey, only the Drennen truly understand them.

  • True faith tolerance: +1 (tolerance_own; raw value 1).

  • Missionary strength: +1% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.01).

3. Face the Axe

“It is true, the orcs are as strong and fearsome as they are cruel. When battle comes, You may feel compelled to turn around and run. But in doing so, you can no longer see the axe of the enemy. The axe you see you can parry, you can dodge, you can break. The axe you do not see will kill you, every time. Face the axe.” -Narawen Drennen

True to her own speech, Narawen did not falter when she came to face Khagur Sapchopper in single combat during the Battle of Drennethílle, striking him with lightning before he was able to bring his axe down on her head. Since then, “Face the axe” has become a common idiom in the Thorn Grove, meaning one stands their ground in the face of danger or hard times.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

4. First Grove of Druids

As Moon Elf became Wood Elf, so too did mage become druid. This first started in Salla Drennen, as the abundance of ambient life magic in the Thorn Grove meant that mages could easily augment magic, tapping into the grove itself to cast spells they had never been able to before. As more mages began to devote themselves to life magic, the first druidic circle was created: The Moonmoss Circle. Their secret grove, Loencyanthanél, is inhabited only by druids seeking to improve and share their magic, taking in young elves from across the Thorn Grove who show magical promise. The Moonmoss Circle has always been a steadfast ally to Salla Drennen, and has produced some of the greatest druids in history.

  • English translation: [Country.GetMageName]: +10% (mages_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.1).

5. Thyr Agoriad

One thousand years… for one thousand years the elves of the Deepwoods struggled in isolation within a feytouched pocket dimension, entrapped by the Verdant Veil. In this time, countless attempts at escape were tried. All failed. Indeed, escape may have been impossible were it not for a fateful encounter with Corin, the Avatar of Agrados. And in her wake came Thyr Agoriad, the Opening.

Lasting from 1443 to the early 1500s, the Opening brought upon countless changes to the remaining Wood Elven clans. From new ways of fighting in the form of Diranbe glaivedancing to the codification of Deepwoods Druidism through Magisterium’s Schools of Magic to simple access to the latest form of the wheeled plow, the period was nothing short of a cultural renaissance. One that may have gone on decades longer were it not for the rise of the Emeraldtide…

  • Goods produced modifier: +5% (global_trade_goods_size_modifier; raw value 0.05).

  • Global institution spread: +20% (global_institution_spread; raw value 0.2).

6. Heralds of a New Age

Every era has its heroes. Names who history remembers met the challenges of their time. Yet, no other time in Wood Elven history can compare to the sheer number to rise during the 15th and 16th centuries - silver tongued Narawen Drennen, ruthless Oberon Fealgarn, bold Alara Cenag, cunning Selussa Ghul, relentless Elaria Ayeth, fearless Faevir Vaytcothyd. It is their legacy that ensured a new age for Wood Elvenkind.

  • General cost: -10% (leader_cost; raw value -0.1).

7. The Oak Oath

The Verdant Pact was the first step to transforming the clans into one state. Yet, by itself, the journey may have ended there; for while defending another clan may have been acceptable, ceding independence to another was not.

Only after the ruinous Emeraldtide, which saw destruction of one clan, the wholesale displacement of another and near wholesale enslavement to the Blackened Prince and his minions, did this attitude change. Having faced true existential destruction, the remaining surviving clans solemnly agreed to gather before the venerable oak where the mother of Wood Elvenkind, Commander Liandel Speardancer was laid to rest. There, for the first time in over a millennium, they elected a new Commander, a Cennasai, to lead the elves of the Deepwoods forward as one state: Cyranvar.

  • Subject liberty desire: +1000% (reduced_liberty_desire; raw value 10).

  • Diplomatic annexation cost: -10% (diplomatic_annexation_cost; raw value -0.1).

Cyranvar (I45) — Cyranvari Ideas

Set ID: I45_ideas_legacy. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Cyranvari Traditions

  • Hostile Attrition: +100% (hostile_attrition; raw value 1).

  • Movement speed: +20% (movement_speed; raw value 0.2).

1. The Grand Opening

Our time in isolation has seen the world change drastically from when our ancestors first entered the shadowed boughs of the Deepwoods. Though we have managed to set aside our petty squabbles and unite, we find ourselves still under threat. We shall open the Deepwoods to the peoples of Cannor so that we might learn from their wisdom lest we stay stuck in our backwards ways and find ourselves threatened beyond our ability to defend.

  • Global institution spread: +25% (global_institution_spread; raw value 0.25).

2. The Green Palace

We have always been a divided people, more prone to tribal or familial loyalties than to any sense of national identity. The invasion of the Deepwoods by the orcish brutes changed that. Our division allowed them to run rampant, ruining the equilibrium of our home and threatening our relationship with the Fey. Now that we have driven out these beasts, and the Verdant Pact has coalesced into a true union of the tribes, we must build a palace truly befitting the High King of the Deepwoods.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

3. One People, One Country

The Greentide beset upon us with a ferocious savagery and those tribes who were too stubborn to join the Verdant Pact found themselves annihilated. Now that the wars have ceased and our homeland is no longer under threat, there are some who mutter about a desire to return to the old ways. However, most have come to see the value of solidarity and realize that the Deepwoods cannot insulate us from the world as it has done in the past. We must become as one people, all willing to sacrifice for our adopted home lest the tides of change sweep us away.

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

4. Between Branches and Leaves

Even in times of peace our people inadvertently prepare for war, for use of the longbow is as much a matter of daily survival as it is for battle. Even the least skilled among us are capable to wielding our ancestral weapon to deadly effect. In times past we would answer the calls of the so often capricious fey and ride to war for some elusive ends. Many of the peoples who borders the Deepwoods still have folk stories warning children that if they misbehave then the fey-folk will steal them away in their sleep. Though it has been centuries, the Escanni saying that it is easier to shoot an arrow through branches and leaves than it is to please the Gods hearkens back to a time when such raids were common. The precision of our ancestors skill continues on to this day.

  • Land fire damage: +15% (fire_damage; raw value 0.15).

5. The Oak Gift

Although the Deepwoods and the fey who inhabit them appear fickle by nature, our ancestors were able to see the pattern of balance underlying all things. From this came our role as stewards and servants of this misunderstood land. Though the woods are just as likely to be bereft of bounty we know that this simply hearkens to a time to come when such things will overflow. Our ability to identify this natural cycle ensures that we never want for goods that we need because we strive to never disrupt the equilibrium of the woods.

  • Goods produced modifier: +10% (global_trade_goods_size_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • National Supply Limit Modifier: +25% (global_supply_limit_modifier; raw value 0.25).

6. The Eyes of the Forest

Though many of our kind have left the safety and comfort of the Deepwoods since their opening hoping to find a better life across Cannor, many of them are actually Eyes of the Forest, sent forth by the High King at the bidding of the fey. They aim to understand the world around us and ensure that a threat like the Greentide is never able to catch our peoples unaware again. The fact that many peoples have an attitude of ingrained dismissiveness towards our kind only makes this task easier; no suspects that beneath the downtrodden visage of a sapling lies the hardened mind of an Eye.

  • Spy network construction: +20% (spy_offence; raw value 0.2).

  • global_spy_defence: +20% (global_spy_defence; raw value 0.2).

7. A Bow in every Home

During the orcish onslaught, our people quickly learned that just as the darkened woodscape veiled us from the world, so too for the greenskins as well. Battles were often swift and brutal and those found unprepared were slaughtered by the invaders. This lesson taught that laxity rests as the worst of sins, for only through preparedness were we able to throw back the orcish tide and save our precious homeland. Should any other threat arise either within or beyond our borders they will find that the once disparate people of Deepwoods are prepared to sacrifice their lives to defend their homeland.

  • Infantry fire: +15% (infantry_fire; raw value 0.15).

Cyranvari Ambition

  • Domestic trade power: +20% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.2).

Cyranvar (I45) — Cyranvari Ideas

Set ID: I45_ideas_elyn. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = I45
        was_tag = I26
    }

Cyranvari Traditions

  • Subject tribute income: +33% (vassal_income; raw value 0.33).

  • Special Unit Force Limit: +10% (special_unit_forcelimit; raw value 0.1).

1. Gather the Conclave

For the Chroniclers in Anbenncóst it is easy to “The unification of elven clans began at the Conclave of Elynaile.” I admit, even in my foolish youth, as I fought with glaive and bow against the invaders, I could feel something changing. All of us could. But, I promise you, we were not one people back then. If we were, then why were there more conclaves?

Trust took time to build. But as Cinrthir later Farwen Elyn gathered the clans time and again to reclaim each grove, I felt myself ever closer to my fellow elf. Knowing we fought for a shared cause of all our choosing bound us tighter than any authority could.

I could not say which conclave was the one that forever tied the clans together. And I promise you no chronicler could either. What I can say is that even today, more than a century after my last soldiering days, those ties still hold. And that they grow ever stronger with each conclave the Ceannasai calls.

  • Vassal force limit contribution: +100% (vassal_forcelimit_bonus; raw value 1).

2. The Oak Oath

It’s funny to me, the things we remember. I couldn’t tell you who I stood by the day we took the first Oak Oath. I don’t remember what I wore or even the day it happened. What I do remember is what my heart felt. Awe, watching the ceanns and ceannas, each heroes of the Greentide in their own right, kneeled before the Ceannasai. Pride, as the Ceannasai, our commander, called us together as one people divided no longer. Resolve, as I and a hundred, no, a thousand others recited the Oath. Ahh, when I close my eyes, I can still hear their voices and my own as one uttering those solemn words:

On the name of my forebears I pledge myself to my fellow elf Blood or no, we are forever kin I pledge to heed without question The word of my Commander Voice and protector of my kin I pledge to forever stand true As the Oak through the turning of season

  • Ruler culture advisor cost: -10% (same_culture_advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • All estates' loyalty equilibrium: +5% (all_estate_loyalty_equilibrium; raw value 0.05).

3. Bond of Silver

Even when I was a Bloomer, barely half a century to my name serving my last years as a ranger, I could not help but notice how the memory of the Veil was quickly fading. Those who were born after did not understand the isolation we older elves had resigned ourselves to. Back then, the woods were wilder. Travel beyond one's grove was a rarity. It was quite the event to just see your cousins in another grove.\N\NAye, I suppose such a time would be impossible to imagine now. With the Veil gone, and especially after the Moon Elves of the Redglades stumbled upon us, the world has opened into a vast expanse. Elves and even humans travel freely hailing Lorent, Anbennar, Celmaldor and beyond. All names that still twist my tongue.

  • Improve relations: +15% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.15).

  • Diplomatic relations: +2 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 2).

4. Thyr Athraythe

The Elders always spoke so highly of the past. I, like so many younger elves, often had to hide my scoffs and eye rolls as they waxed and waned about how the previous century had been so much better. Yet now that I have seen nearly two hundred years myself, I can’t help but curse the folly of youth.

The history books call it the Rebirth, Tyr Athraythe in our own tongue. For me, though, it was simply a happier time. After spending my years as a Sapling at war, I found a life beyond it - potion making. Indeed so too did many of my kin find joy in peace. Neighboring my shop were stores offering all sorts of goods once restricted to the grove they came from. Wine from the Lake Grove, ivory carvings from the Bone Grove, spices and herbs (perfect for potions) from the Flower Grove. Indeed, in exchange for my rather excellent potions, I found myself never enough bottles of fine Chilac wine, too many racks full of reagents, and, eventually, something priceless - love.

  • Goods produced modifier: +15% (global_trade_goods_size_modifier; raw value 0.15).

5. At the Center of Three Worlds

The thing about outsiders is how they always gawk when they come to our lands. I don’t blame them, I suppose. Turns out our sort of normal isn’t like theirs. Your average Moon Elf can’t take a bite of (much less appreciate) boiled bark. For all their bluster, dwarves aren’t used to screaming at the local boggles for tearing up the field. And good luck finding a human who can handle a satyr.

Of course that goes both ways. As my little shop grew into something bigger, I met all sorts of strange folk I learned to call friends. Lyra of Turnmarket, a Corinite Greave from Stalbor was an excellent customer who never ceased to tell tales of crimson rain and Corin’s cause. Madarûn Ironbeard, a dwarf “merchant” (I always suspected a smuggler, but ignorance is a valuable thing) who always seemed to be both on the in and out of every cartel in the Serpentspine. And, of course, Jaddarésa Bedavírar, a harpy named after the daughter of the fabled first Herald of the Jadd Empire. A fact she insisted on telling me and every customer. Seelie Queen smile upon her, in all my years, never have I met someone as sweet and dogged as her. Forty years and she still tries to bring the light of the Jadd to my life.

  • Domestic trade power: +20% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.2).

6. Ash Children

By the time those feyscorned guns made their way to Cyranvar, my days as a soldier were long behind me. The same could not be said for my wayward daughter. When I look back, I feel pride. Her skill as a sharpshooter easily outclassed my own and her sense of duty toward our people mirrored my own when the forest was still divided between the clans. But at the time, I could only shake my head in disapproval. She and her cohort acted like any sapling would, rebellious and brash. They needed a stern hand to correct this.

To my then bafflement, the Ceannacai encouraged this new generation’s behavior. Dubbing them Ash Children, they were marched to battle equipped with those ructious weapons. Gone were the simple days of the bow and glaive. It was a new era, one filled with bellowing smoke, manic war cries, and neverending cacophony of fire.

  • Infantry fire: +15% (infantry_fire; raw value 0.15).

7. The War of the Black Tower

Something said can never be unsaid. And after words not worth repeating, my daughter left my shop. Fury gripped me at first, but when she did not return, anger chilled to sorrow. I could not find her, and so I gave myself to my work. Built a mercantile empire dedicated to tracking my lost scion. I did not care when the War of Treachery began. I paid no heed as Esthil and its Witch-Queen lich rose the dead to fight their perverse war.

Even as the old elven clans who had settled Escann warned of the growing threat, not a word could reach my ears. It was only when a young man carrying a shattered sword showed up to my step was I shaken from stupor. At my first sight, and to my shame, all I saw was the union of an elf… and an orc. It was only when I locked eyes with him did I see him for who he was, not simply what.

He was Elrac of Dustandar, proud member of Arturos’ Watch. And he was my grandson.

I cannot begin to express my regrets here. Nor is there time. Elrac, just as his mother, and perhaps just as this old elf was, is driven by sworn duty. No… I remember my oath well. Evil is ascendent and my kin are in need. I will organize an audience for Elrac with the Ceannacai. Cyranvar and its commander must act.

  • Army tradition: +1 (army_tradition; raw value 1).

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

Cyranvari Ambition

  • Promoted culture development cost: -10% (development_cost_in_primary_culture; raw value -0.1).

Cyranvar (I45) — Cyranvari Ideas

Set ID: I45_ideas_drennen. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Cyranvari Traditions

  • Improve relations: +10% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Religious power modifier: +20% (church_power_modifier; raw value 0.2).

1. Face the Axe

Anyone who hasn’t felt the fear of battle’s eve is either a fool or a dead elf walking in my eyes. Once you behold the sight of an orcish host, hear the howls of their warcries, feel the tension of simply waiting for the blood to spill - it gnaws at the spirit. The fear becomes heavy, a weight that threatens to break you before the first arrow has been loosed.

I’m certain when Narawen Drennen turned to address us, she felt it too. How else could the then Ceanna of Salla Drennen have spoken with such conviction? Even now, a century later and her words still ring in my ears.

“Turn not from the foe, for the foe you cannot see will strike you dead. Turn not from your fear, for the fear you do not know will beat you broken. Face your foe, face your fear. Face the axe.“

  • morale_damage_received: -10% (morale_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

2. The Oak Oath

It’s funny to me, the things we remember. I couldn’t tell you who I stood by the day we took the first Oak Oath. I don’t remember what I wore or even the day it happened. What I do remember is what my heart felt. Awe, watching the ceanns and ceannas, each heroes of the Greentide in their own right, kneeled before the Ceannasai. Pride, as the Ceannasai, our commander, called us together as one people divided no longer. Resolve, as I and a hundred, no, a thousand others recited the Oath. Ahh, when I close my eyes, I can still hear their voices and my own as one uttering those solemn words:

On the name of my forebears I pledge myself to my fellow elf Blood or no, we are forever kin I pledge to heed without question The word of my Commander Voice and protector of my kin I pledge to forever stand true As the Oak through the turning of season

  • Ruler culture advisor cost: -10% (same_culture_advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • All estates' loyalty equilibrium: +5% (all_estate_loyalty_equilibrium; raw value 0.05).

3. How It's Done

I am no druid. As the Cannorians say, I lack “the spark” of magic. However, that doesn’t mean I am ignorant of it or the bounties it’s given the elves of Cyranvar.

It was magic that renewed the Veil and smoothed the tear between our realm and the fey’s. It was magic that brought the verdant blooms of plants and crops. It was magic that began the end of the wars. After all, it was no blade that killed Khagur Sapchopper - but a bolt of lightning.

4. Thyr Athraythe

The Elders always spoke so highly of the past. I, like so many younger elves, often had to hide my scoffs and eye rolls as they waxed and waned about how the previous century had been so much better. Yet now that I have seen nearly two hundred years myself, I can’t help but curse the folly of youth.

The history books call it the Rebirth, Tyr Athraythe in our own tongue. For me, though, it was simply a happier time. After spending my years as a Sapling at war, I found a life beyond it - potion making. Indeed so too did many of my kin find joy in peace. Neighboring my shop were stores offering all sorts of goods once restricted to the grove they came from. Wine from the Lake Grove, ivory carvings from the Bone Grove, spices and herbs (perfect for potions) from the Flower Grove. Indeed, in exchange for my rather excellent potions, I found myself never enough bottles of fine Chilac wine, too many racks full of reagents, and, eventually, something priceless - love.

The thing about outsiders is how they always gawk when they come to our lands. I don’t blame them, I suppose. Turns out our sort of normal isn’t like theirs. 6. Ash Children

By the time those feyscorned guns made their way to Cyranvar, my days as a soldier were long behind me. The same could not be said for my wayward daughter. When I look back, I feel pride. Her skill as a sharpshooter easily outclassed my own and her sense of duty toward our people mirrored my own when the forest was still divided between the clans. But at the time, I could only shake my head in disapproval. She and her cohort acted like any sapling would, rebellious and brash. They needed a stern hand to correct this.

7. The War of the Black Tower

Something said can never be unsaid. And after words not worth repeating, my daughter left my shop. Fury gripped me at first, but when she did not return, anger chilled to sorrow. I could not find her, and so I gave myself to my work. Built a mercantile empire dedicated to tracking my lost scion. I did not care when the War of Treachery began. I paid no heed as Esthil and its Witch-Queen lich rose the dead to fight their perverse war.

Even as the old elven clans who had settled Escann warned of the growing threat, not a word could reach my ears. It was only when a young man carrying a shattered sword showed up to my step was I shaken from stupor. At my first sight, and to my shame, all I saw was the union of an elf… and an orc. It was only when I locked eyes with him did I see him for who he was, not simply what.

He was Elrac of Dustandar, proud member of Arturos’ Watch. And he was my grandson.

I cannot begin to express my regrets here. Nor is there time. Elrac, just as his mother, and perhaps just as this old elf was, is driven by sworn duty. No… I remember my oath well. Evil is ascendent and my kin are in need. I will organize an audience for Elrac with the Ceannacai. Cyranvar and its commander must act.

1. Face the Arrow

When it comes to spilling blood, no one ever comes out clean. Anyone fighting a war is quick to learn that lesson. What I didn’t realize was how much worse it could get. It wasn’t until my fellow rangers and I fell under Elaria Ayeth’s command that I learned how far the depravities of war go.

Blind all but one survivor so that they may lead their maimed comrades back to their chieftain. Burn the foe’s fields but not their homes so that they may know the dying pain of starvation. Strike at all times so that they may never know respite, so that they fear even the shadows and sway of the leaves. Break their spirits so they pray to whatever power they wish for escape. Then… teach them the final lesson. “There is no escape in the end, all must Face the Arrow.”

That is all I have to say of that. I wish to consider those times no more.

1. Auralarn Academy

My daughter’s favorites were always those of the huntsmen and huntresses of Auralarn Academy. Imagine the threat of the Greentide and promise of the Verdant Pact being swallowed whole by something far greater. Where the fey you have lived with your life become warped and disfigured. And as a heart of darkness threatens to swallow you and all you hold dear whole, only for a red-hooded figure atop a Fealgarn Stag to suddenly appear and strike down the Warped Fey. A dozen other mounted warriors charging through and scattering the creatures. The figure gives a smile of reassurance then rides on to save the day and live happily ever after.

Or so the story goes that I told my daughter. All but the end, I can claim validity. Though I never did see that red-hood again, I wish to believe she, the huntsmen, and the huntresses that saved us that day saw a hero’s ending.

1. Aerial Countercharges

The giant hawks of the Mountain Grove… Certainly they and their riders are famous now, but back then? When I first heard of Bricena Myna’s flight my first reaction was to laugh. Who would be bold enough face down a bird twice the size of an elf much less ride it? If there was such an elf, it was certainly not the ceanna renowned for poise and grace. With jeer, I dismissed the story as just another attempt to sprinkle fairie dust in my eyes by my fellow rangers. By the grace of Seelie and resolve of the Unseelie, I remain ever grateful to have been proven wrong.

Despite having faced an orcish charge two dozen a time, me and my fellow rangers found ourselves scattered. I fully admit to the fear that struck me. To having thoughts of fleeing as disaster struck us. But such fears were crushed, just as the orc that nearly took my head was beneath the talon of a great eagle. I never had the chance to thank my rescuer. They had taken off before I could even gain my bearings. Despite that, my comrades never stopped squawking it was Bricena herself who saved me. A jest I will grudgingly tolerate for my life.

2. The Oak Oath

It’s funny to me, the things we remember. I couldn’t tell you who I stood by the day we took the first Oak Oath. I don’t remember what I wore or even the day it happened. What I do remember is what my heart felt. Awe, watching the ceanns and ceannas, each heroes of the Greentide in their own right, kneeled before the Ceannasai. Pride, as the Ceannasai, our commander, called us together as one people divided no longer. Resolve, as I and a hundred, no, a thousand others recited the Oath. Ahh, when I close my eyes, I can still hear their voices and my own as one uttering those solemn words:

On the name of my forebears I pledge myself to my fellow elf Blood or no, we are forever kin I pledge to heed without question The word of my Commander Voice and protector of my kin I pledge to forever stand true As the Oak through the turning of season

3. Shared Projects

For all of its claims, Elynaile will never hold the same splendor in my eyes as Ciranmyna. No matter what the elves of the Lake Grove say, every elf knows what city shines as the jewel of the forest. And if there had been any room for doubt before Bricena’s reign, those doubts were well dismissed by its end. Drennen druidship, Ayeth architecture, Ahain silver… the city contains the works of each clan in multitudes. The city truly stands as a testament to the shared work of the salla, even before Cyranvar came to be. Even to this day, as I stroll the winding streets, I can spy members of each Great Salla still eagerly working together to build something even greater.

4. Thyr Athraythe

The Elders always spoke so highly of the past. I, like so many younger elves, often had to hide my scoffs and eye rolls as they waxed and waned about how the previous century had been so much better. Yet now that I have seen nearly two hundred years myself, I can’t help but curse the folly of youth.

The history books call it the Rebirth, Tyr Athraythe in our own tongue. For me, though, it was simply a happier time. After spending my years as a Sapling at war, I found a life beyond it - potion making. Indeed so too did many of my kin find joy in peace. Neighboring my shop were stores offering all sorts of goods once restricted to the grove they came from. Wine from the Lake Grove, ivory carvings from the Bone Grove, spices and herbs (perfect for potions) from the Flower Grove. Indeed, in exchange for my rather excellent potions, I found myself never enough bottles of fine Chilac wine, too many racks full of reagents, and, eventually, something priceless - love.

5. At the Center of Three Worlds

The thing about outsiders is how they always gawk when they come to our lands. I don’t blame them, I suppose. Turns out our sort of normal isn’t like theirs. Your average Moon Elf can’t take a bite of (much less appreciate) boiled bark. For all their bluster, dwarves aren’t used to screaming at the local boggles for tearing up the field. And good luck finding a human who can handle a satyr.

Of course that goes both ways. As my little shop grew into something bigger, I met all sorts of strange folk I learned to call friends. Lyra of Turnmarket, a Corinite Greave from Stalbor was an excellent customer who never ceased to tell tales of crimson rain and Corin’s cause. Madarûn Ironbeard, a dwarf “merchant” (I always suspected a smuggler, but ignorance is a valuable thing) who always seemed to be both on the in and out of every cartel in the Serpentspine. And, of course, Jaddarésa Bedavírar, a harpy named after the daughter of the fabled first Herald of the Jadd Empire. A fact she insisted on telling me and every customer. Seelie Queen smile upon her, in all my years, never have I met someone as sweet and dogged as her. Forty years and she still tries to bring the light of the Jadd to my life.

6. Ash Children

By the time those feyscorned guns made their way to Cyranvar, my days as a soldier were long behind me. The same could not be said for my wayward daughter. When I look back, I feel pride. Her skill as a sharpshooter easily outclassed my own and her sense of duty toward our people mirrored my own when the forest was still divided between the clans. But at the time, I could only shake my head in disapproval. She and her cohort acted like any sapling would, rebellious and brash. They needed a stern hand to correct this.

To my then bafflement, the Ceannacai encouraged this new generation’s behavior. Dubbing them Ash Children, they were marched to battle equipped with those ructious weapons. Gone were the simple days of the bow and glaive. It was a new era, one filled with bellowing smoke, manic war cries, and neverending cacophony of fire.
